info.title: alexia-familia-api
info.summary: A REST API for the Alexia Familia parent portal
info.description:
An unofficial JSON API for the Alexia Familia parent portal. You run it yourself. It signs in to your own account and serves what the school shows you about your children.

**Keys.** Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or in the `X-API-Key` header. Make keys with `alexia-api keys create`. A key holds scopes (`read`, `write`, `admin`, `feed`) and a list of accounts it may use. The calendar feeds also take a key that holds only the `feed` scope as `?key=`, because a calendar app cannot send a header.

**Caching.** The server keeps each answer for a short time so that it stays gentle with the school's system. The `X-Cache` and `Age` headers say how an answer was found. Add `fresh=true` to ask the portal again.

**Errors.** Every failure is an RFC 9457 problem document with a stable `code` and a `request_id`. A 503 means the account cannot be used until the operator acts, for example after a wrong password. A 502 or a 504 means the portal misbehaved or did not answer.

get.description: Names the server and says where its documentation and health checks are.

get.summary: Report that the process is alive
get.description: Answers 200 whenever the process runs. It does not look at the portal, the accounts, or the key file, so a container can use it as a liveness check. It answers for any host name, even when `allowed_hosts` is set, because a platform probes with its own address.

get.summary: Report whether the server can serve requests
get.description: Answers 200 when at least one account and at least one API key are configured, the key file can be read, and the state directory is writable. Otherwise it answers 503 and names the checks that failed. It never calls the portal. It answers for any host name, like the liveness check.

get.summary: List the accounts this key may use
get.description: Needs the `read` scope. It lists the accounts the key is allowed to use, with the state of each connection. It never calls the portal, so it is cheap and safe to poll.
Needs the `read` scope. It shows the state of the connection, which switches the operator turned on, and how many children the last login listed. It never calls the portal.

get.summary: Show the agenda of a child
get.description: Needs the `read` scope. Gives the lessons and the school events of one child for a range of days, earliest first. `from` and `to` are days at the school, written YYYY-MM-DD, and both count. Without them the range is today and the six days after it. A range covers at most 366 days and lies within 1100 days of today. A range that breaks these rules, or that ends before it starts, is refused with the code `invalid_window`. A lesson names its teacher and carries the numbers the school flagged for it, which are tasks, activities, notes, and tests, and whether a substitute teacher takes it. A holiday is a school event whose title the school writes as `festivo`. A time has the offset the school has on that day, so it reads the same on both sides of a clock change. The portal answers a range with far more than was asked for, so the server keeps only the days you asked for. Each range is stored on its own for a while, and `fresh=true` reads it again. The portal shows one agenda at a time for a login, so this read waits for the other requests of the same account.

get.summary: Subscribe to the calendar of a child
get.description: Needs the `feed` scope, which every other scope includes. Gives an iCalendar file that a calendar app can subscribe to, with the lessons, the school events, and the holidays of one child. It reaches back `back` days and ahead `ahead` days from today at the school, and it lists lessons only for the next `lessons_ahead` days. A holiday or any other entry that lasts all day shows as free time. A lesson says its teacher and what the school flagged for it. Calendar apps cannot send a header, so this route also takes the key as `?key=`, but only a key that holds nothing but the `feed` scope. Make one with `alexia-api keys create NAME --scope feed`. A key with another scope is refused in a URL even when it is right, so an address that leaks opens calendars and nothing else. There is no `fresh` option, because this address is meant to be handed to other software. When the portal cannot be read, the answer is a problem and not a shorter calendar, so an app keeps what it had.

get.summary: Subscribe to one calendar for the whole family
get.description: Needs the `feed` scope, which every other scope includes. Gives one iCalendar file with the lessons and school events of every child of the account and the guardian's interviews. Each entry of a child starts with the child's first name, or with the first name and the slug when two children share a first name. A holiday that the whole school shares appears once and has no name in front of it. Lessons stop after `lessons_ahead` days, as for a single child. The file is all or nothing, so one child whose agenda cannot be read fails the whole file, and a calendar app does not take the missing entries for entries that the school removed. Calendar apps cannot send a header, so this route also takes the key as `?key=`, but only a key that holds nothing but the `feed` scope. Make one with `alexia-api keys create NAME --scope feed`. A key with another scope is refused in a URL even when it is right, so an address that leaks opens calendars and nothing else. There is no `fresh` option, because this address is meant to be handed to other software. When the portal cannot be read, the answer is a problem and not a shorter calendar, so an app keeps what it had.

get.summary: List the messages in a folder
get.description: Needs the `read` scope. Messages come newest first, a page at a time. The portal belongs to the guardian and not to a child, so the list holds the messages for every child of the account. The server reads the whole folder from the portal once and stores it, so paging through it costs the portal a single read. Ask with `fresh=true` to see a message that arrived a moment ago.

get.description: Needs the `read` scope. Gives the message as the list shows it, together with when the school sent it, its words, the addresses in them, and its files. The message must be in the list of the folder you name, so a message the family sent needs `folder=sent`. `body.html` is safe to show, and `body.text` holds the same words as plain text. The server stores a message after it reads it, so asking again is cheap. `fresh=true` reads the message again, and the list of its folder too. Opening a message in the portal may mark it as read there, and this server cannot tell whether it does. The `read` field comes from the list, so it shows the state from before the message was opened.

get.summary: Download one file of a message
get.description: Needs the `read` scope. Gives the bytes of one file that the `attachments` of the message list. The server fetches the file from the portal every time and keeps nothing, so you always get the file as it is now. The message must be in the list of the folder you name, so a message the family sent needs `folder=sent`. A file larger than the operator's `max_attachment_mib` is refused with a 413 and the code `attachment_too_large`. The portal sends every file as a plain stream of bytes, so the `Content-Type` is judged from the first bytes of the file. A web page or a vector picture is never named as one. It comes as `text/plain`, so a client that shows a file by its type cannot be made to run it. The answer always asks the client to save the file. `fresh=true` reads the list of the message's folder again, which a message that arrived a moment ago needs.

id.title: Id
id.description: The account's short name in URLs, chosen by the operator.

label.title: Label
label.description: A name for people, for example the guardian's first name. It also names the family calendar and the guardian calendar.

portal_host.title: Portal Host
portal_host.description: The host name of the portal this account signs in to.

child_count.title: Child Count
child_count.description: Children seen at the last login, or null before the first login.

Account.title: Account
Account.description: One set of portal credentials. It holds the children that the portal lists for it.

from.title: From
from.description: The first day of the range, inclusive. It is the day that was asked for.

to.title: To
to.description: The last day of the range, inclusive.

items.title: Items
items.description: The entries that touch the range, earliest first, with the kinds asked for.

Agenda.title: Agenda
Agenda.description: The entries of an agenda over a range of days, in the order they happen.

id.title: Id
id.description: Names this occurrence and no other. The portal gives a lesson the same id every week, so this id is the portal's id, a `|`, and the day, as in `<id>|2026-10-19`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `lesson` for a lesson of the timetable, `interview` for a meeting with a teacher, `holiday` for a school event that the school titles `festivo`, and `school_event` for everything else the school puts in the agenda.

title.title: Title
title.description: The title as the school writes it, in the school's language.

teacher.title: Teacher
teacher.description: The teacher the portal names for the entry, or null when it names none.

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: When the entry starts, with the school's offset. The portal writes local time and marks it as UTC by mistake, and this server puts the right offset on it.

ends_at.title: Ends At
ends_at.description: When the entry ends, with the school's offset.

all_day.title: All Day
all_day.description: True when the entry covers whole days. The portal gives such an entry the times 00:00 and 00:00 or 23:59, and the days it covers run from `starts_at` to `ends_at`.

signals.description: What the school flags on a lesson. Null for any other kind of entry.

AgendaEvent.title: AgendaEvent
AgendaEvent.description: One entry of the school agenda.

id.title: Id
id.description: A token that names the file within its message. Treat it as opaque. It is safe to put in a URL path, and the download address of the file ends with it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The file's name as the sender gave it.

size.title: Size
size.description: The file's size in bytes, as the portal lists it.

Attachment.title: Attachment
Attachment.description: A file that came with a message.

cause.title: Cause
cause.description: The failure that paused automatic logins.

interstitial.title: Interstitial
interstitial.description: The portal page that needs a person, when the cause is a required step.

Blocked.title: Blocked
Blocked.description:
Automatic logins are paused until an operator resets the block.

A wrong password can lock a guardian's account, so the server stops after the first login
failure that could do that and waits for a person to fix the cause.

html.title: Html
html.description: The message as HTML that is safe to show. Scripts, styles, forms, frames, and event handlers are gone, and so are classes and inline styles. A link keeps only an `http`, `https`, `mailto`, or `tel` address. An image stays only when the message carries it inline as a PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP picture.

text.title: Text
text.description: The message as plain text. A blank line separates paragraphs. A list item starts with `- `, or with its number and a dot in a numbered list, and a list inside a list is indented by two spaces. Table cells in a row are separated by ` | `. A link shows its address in parentheses after its words.

simplified.title: Simplified
simplified.description: True when the message was nested too deeply to read as HTML. Then `html` holds only the words of the message, in one paragraph.

Body.title: Body
Body.description: The words of a message, as safe HTML and as plain text.

writes.title: Writes
writes.description: Messages and meeting requests may be sent through the outbox.

forms.title: Forms
forms.description: Forms may be answered. This needs writes as well.

restore_unread.title: Restore Unread
restore_unread.description: A message opened through the API is put back to unread at the portal.

Capabilities.title: Capabilities
Capabilities.description: What the operator switched on for an account.

id.title: Id
id.description: The portal's student id. Most per-child calls use it, and so do URLs.

person_id.title: Person Id
person_id.description: The portal's person id for the child. The agenda and the photo use it.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: A short name for URLs, made from the first name. The operator can pin it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The full name as the portal shows it.

relation.title: Relation
relation.description: How the portal labels the relation to the guardian, when it shows one.

Child.title: Child
Child.description: One child of the signed-in guardian.

session.title: Session
session.description: Whether the server had to log in, or the session it had still worked.

child_count.title: Child Count
child_count.description: How many children the login lists.

ConnectionCheck.title: ConnectionCheck
ConnectionCheck.description: The result of making sure the account has a working portal session.

was_blocked.title: Was Blocked
was_blocked.description: Whether logins had been paused before the reset.

ConnectionReset.title: ConnectionReset
ConnectionReset.description: The result of lifting a block.

location.title: Location
location.description: Where the problem is, for example ["query", "fresh"].

FieldProblem.title: FieldProblem
FieldProblem.description: One thing wrong with the request, and where it was.

name.title: Name
name.description: `received` or `sent`. The message routes take this name.

label.title: Label
label.description: The folder's name as the portal shows it, in the school's language.

count.title: Count
count.description: The number the portal prints next to the folder's name, or null when it prints none. Treat it as a hint. The message list reports the exact total.

Folder.title: Folder
Folder.description: A folder of messages, as the portal lists it.

Health.title: Health
Health.description: The process is up. This says nothing about the portal.

docs.title: Docs
docs.description: The interactive documentation, or null when it is off.

openapi.title: Openapi
openapi.description: The OpenAPI document, or null when it is off.

Index.title: Index
Index.description: Where things are on this server.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.description: Homework and tasks tied to the lesson.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Teacher notes tied to the lesson.

tests.title: Tests
tests.description: Tests and quizzes tied to the lesson.

substitution.title: Substitution
substitution.description: True when a substitute teacher takes the lesson.

LessonSignals.title: LessonSignals
LessonSignals.description: What the school flags on one lesson. A zero or a false means that nothing is flagged.

url.title: Url
url.description: The address as the message writes it.

host.title: Host
host.description: The host the address points to, without a leading `www.`. For a mail address, the part after the `@`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What the address is for, judged from its host and its file name. `other` when it is none of the kinds this API knows.

Link.title: Link
Link.description: An address that a message mentions, in a link or in its words.

last_success_at.title: Last Success At
last_success_at.description: When the portal last answered a call.

LoggedIn.title: LoggedIn
LoggedIn.description: A session is open and the portal answered it recently.

LoggedOut.title: LoggedOut
LoggedOut.description: No session is open. The next request that needs the portal logs in first.

id.title: Id
id.description: The portal's message id. The detail and attachment routes take it.

read.title: Read
read.description: Whether the guardian has read the message, or null when the portal's icon is not one this API knows.

institutional.title: Institutional
institutional.description: True for a message sent in the school's own name.

sender.title: Sender
sender.description: The sender's name as the portal shows it.

received_on.title: Received On
received_on.description: The day the portal lists the message under, on the school's calendar.

expires_on.title: Expires On
expires_on.description: The last day the portal shows the message, when it has one.

anonymous.title: Anonymous
anonymous.description: True when the portal marks the message as anonymous.

category.title: Category
category.description: The category the portal files the message under.

has_attachments.title: Has Attachments
has_attachments.description: True when the portal shows a paperclip.

sent_at.title: Sent At
sent_at.description: When the school sent the message, to the minute, with the school's offset. The list gives only a day, and the time comes from the message itself.

links.title: Links
links.description: The addresses in the body, each once. The ones in links come first, then the ones written out in the words. Translations are not searched.

translations.title: Translations
translations.description: Other versions of the message, second before third. Empty when there are none.

child_names.title: Child Names
child_names.description: The names of the children the portal says the message is about, in the one text the portal writes them in, or null when it names none. The portal gives names and no ids, so this API cannot tie them to its list of children.

can_reply.title: Can Reply
can_reply.description: Whether the portal offers a reply to this message.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: A message with its words. The fields of its row in the list come first.

total.title: Total
total.description: How many messages match, counting every page. It counts the messages this server holds, which is fewer than the portal lists when `truncated` is true.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: The page size that was asked for.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: How many matching messages come before this page.

next_offset.title: Next Offset
next_offset.description: The offset to ask for the next page, or null on the last page.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True when the folder is longer than this server reads. The newest messages are here and the oldest are left out.

MessagePage.title: MessagePage
MessagePage.description: One page of the messages in a folder, newest first.

id.title: Id
id.description: The portal's message id. The detail and attachment routes take it.

read.title: Read
read.description: Whether the guardian has read the message, or null when the portal's icon is not one this API knows.

institutional.title: Institutional
institutional.description: True for a message sent in the school's own name.

sender.title: Sender
sender.description: The sender's name as the portal shows it.

received_on.title: Received On
received_on.description: The day the portal lists the message under, on the school's calendar.

expires_on.title: Expires On
expires_on.description: The last day the portal shows the message, when it has one.

anonymous.title: Anonymous
anonymous.description: True when the portal marks the message as anonymous.

category.title: Category
category.description: The category the portal files the message under.

has_attachments.title: Has Attachments
has_attachments.description: True when the portal shows a paperclip.

MessageSummary.title: MessageSummary
MessageSummary.description: A message as the portal lists it, without its text.

type.title: Type
type.description: Always about:blank. Use `code`, which is stable, to tell problems apart.

title.title: Title
title.description: The standard name of the HTTP status.

status.title: Status
status.description: The HTTP status of the response.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: What went wrong and what to do about it, for a person.

code.title: Code
code.description: A stable name for the problem. Branch on this, not on text.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Quote this when you report a bug.

cause.title: Cause
cause.description: Why logins are paused, when the account is blocked.

since.title: Since
since.description: When logins were paused, when the account is blocked.

interstitial.title: Interstitial
interstitial.description: The portal page that wants a person, in a browser.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Which of the operator's switches refused the call.

needed.title: Needed
needed.description: The scope the key would need, when it lacks one.

retry_after_seconds.title: Retry After Seconds
retry_after_seconds.description: How long to wait before asking again, when rate limited.

errors.title: Errors
errors.description: The parts of the request that are not valid.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. Members past `request_id` appear only when they apply.

checks.title: Checks
checks.description: One entry per thing that was checked.

Readiness.title: Readiness
Readiness.description: Whether the server can serve requests. It never calls the portal.

id.title: Id
id.description: The portal's employee id. Meeting requests use it.

role.title: Role
role.description: The role the portal prints after the name, if any.

StaffMember.title: StaffMember
StaffMember.description: A teacher or other staff member who can meet with the guardian about a child.

TrackingCounters.title: TrackingCounters
TrackingCounters.description: The numbers in the portal's tracking widget for one child.

slot.title: Slot
slot.description: The portal keeps up to three versions of a message and does not name their languages. The message itself is the first version, so a translation is the second or the third.

Translation.title: Translation
Translation.description: The message in another language, when the sender wrote one.

BearerKey.description: An API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Make one with `alexia-api keys create`.

HeaderKey.description: An API key, sent in the `X-API-Key` header. Use it when a client cannot set `Authorization`.
HeaderKey.name: X-API-Key

FeedKey.description: A key that holds only the `feed` scope, sent as `?key=<key>`. Use it for a calendar app that cannot set a header. Make one with `alexia-api keys create NAME --scope feed`. A key with any other scope is refused here.
FeedKey.name: key

tags.name: meta
tags.description: Is the server up, and where is everything.

tags.name: accounts
tags.description: The portal accounts this server holds, and their state.

tags.name: children
tags.description: The children of an account and their school data.

tags.name: agenda
tags.description: The lessons, interviews, and school events of each child and of the guardian, as data and as calendar files that a calendar app can subscribe to.

tags.name: messages
tags.description: The message folders of an account and the messages in them.
